title: Private inference networking - SLAB pilot notes
content:
Context:
Customer: SLAB Systems (regulated fintech). Running sensitive model inference on private deployment (Redwood Private) inside their AWS account. They requested a low-risk network approach: no internet-facing ENIs on inference hosts, stricter egress controls, auditability, and ability to fail closed to a stub model when connectivity to Redwood control plane is lost.

Primary goals:
- Ensure model serving instances have no public ingress (no public ENIs).
- Provide controlled outbound connectivity for: metrics, logs, control-plane heartbeats, container image pulls (initial bootstrap), and occasional updates.
- Support split-horizon DNS so model endpoints resolve to private IPs inside SLAB VPC and to public endpoints for dev sandbox.
- Keep latency to <35ms p50 for intra-region control-plane calls.
- Provide clear rollback and isolation steps for security review.

Constraints from SLAB security review:
- Must avoid long-lived NAT IPs shared with other teams / accounts.
- Egress must be restricted to an allowlist of IPs and hostnames owned by Redwood and a small set of third-party SaaS (Datadog, S3).
- TLS mutual auth for control-plane webhook endpoints is preferred (mTLS).
- VPC peering is allowed but VPC-to-VPC transitive routing is not (no TGW in initial phase).
- Host-level outbound firewall (iptables) allowed on inference nodes.

Three candidate patterns evaluated (short):
1) VPC peering + NAT Gateway per AZ + outgoing allowlist.
   - Pros: simple, supported, low operational friction for SLAB.
   - Cons: NAT cost, NAT IPs change on replacement, need to manage route propagation and security group references.
2) Interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to Redwood control-plane + proxy egress via customer side HTTP proxy -> allowlist by hostname + IP for third-party services.
   - Pros: No public IPs seen by instances, fine-grained control, lower surface area for AWS-managed services.
   - Cons: Requires Redwood to publish PrivateLink NLBs in partner account or accept cross-account endpoint services; more setup and SLA coordination.
3) Egress through dedicated egress VPC with static Elastic IPs + explicit routing via peering + customer-managed forward proxy (squid) for hostname allowlist.
   - Pros: Static, auditable IPs; central place to apply WAF/IDS.
   - Cons: More components, potential single point of failure (mitigated by HA pair).

Customer-chosen approach (consensus):
Hybrid: Primary = PrivateLink for control-plane and metrics, Secondary = NAT Gateway for S3/image pulls and third-party SaaS. Reason: SLAB prioritized no public-facing control-plane traffic and strong hostname-based allowlist for Redwood endpoints; they accepted NAT for limited egress to S3 and Datadog.

Detailed design notes:
- VPC topology:
  - SLAB VPC-A (private subnets for inference) - no public subnets used for inference.
  - PrivateLink endpoints (Interface endpoints) created in each AZ's private subnet for: redwood-controlplane.grpc.redwood.example (contains mTLS cert negotiation). Endpoint ENIs get private IPs from subnet CIDR.
  - S3 gateway endpoint for fetching model artifacts (preferred over NAT for large pulls) - note: customer requested to avoid pulling model layers over NAT where possible to save costs.
  - NAT Gateway(s): reserved for non-PrivateLink egress (image registry, Datadog). Use 2 NAT Gateways in separate AZs with route table per private subnet with AZ affinity.

DNS plan (split horizon):
- SLAB will run Route53 private hosted zone: redwood-controlplane.internal.example -> maps to interface endpoint ENIs.
- For dev sandbox (public) we leave public DNS pointing to Redwood public control plane. Engineers will toggle resolver suffix or use conditional forwarding when testing.
- Important: TTLs for redwood hostnames set to 60s during rollout to allow fast flip.
- Validate: 'dig +short redwood-controlplane.internal.example @10.0.0.2' (customer resolver IP) should return private ENI IPs.

Egress & security controls:
- mTLS for all control-plane RPCs; Redwood will provide client cert bundle for SLAB to trust. Certificate rotation window: 30 days before expiry.
- Customer requested outbound allowlist: redwood-controlplane.*, s3.amazonaws.com (only via S3 endpoint), api.datadoghq.com:443 (NAT egress). Provide expected IP ranges for Datadog as part of runbook.
- OS hardening: turn on host firewall rules to only allow outbound to: PrivateLink endpoints IPs, NAT GW IPs, and S3 endpoints (via VPC endpoint).
- Health probes: Redwood runtime will probe control-plane on /health with mutual TLS every 10s with 2s timeout. Failure threshold: 3 consecutive failures -> model fallback logic triggers to local stub model.

Endpoint considerations and AWS limits:
- Interface endpoints have ENI quotas; advise requesting quota increase to avoid hitting 50 ENI-per-subnet soft limits when scaling to many AZs.
- AWS PrivateLink supports 55 Gbps per ENI (varies); run synthetic throughput tests during POC.
- S3 Gateway endpoints do not use ENIs and are billed differently.

Operational checklist (POC playbook):
1) Pre-reqs (customer): create cross-account role for Redwood infra to verify endpoint/service acceptance (optional).
2) Create private hosted zone and attach to SLAB VPC.
3) Provision Interface Endpoints (one per AZ). Document ENI IDs and private IPs.
4) Configure route tables for private subnets (ensure no 0.0.0.0/0 to IGW). Verify no public IPs on inference host ENIs.
5) Create S3 gateway endpoint for the model bucket and update IAM policy to restrict access to the bucket prefix used for this POC.
6) Spin up a small canary cluster (1 node per AZ) with Redwood Private agent and point to PrivateLink control-plane hostname.
7) Validate TLS handshake logs and mTLS certificate acceptance.
8) Exercise model pull using aws s3 cp via endpoint; measure sustained throughput and tail latencies.
9) Configure NAT Gateway and egress-only route for image pulls; test egress to Datadog.
10) Run synthetic latency tests for control-plane calls and verify p50/p95 are within SLO.

Testing checklist (quick):
- DNS: private resolution correct -> list ENI IPs returned.
- TLS: mTLS negotiated; client cert subject matches 'redwood-client:slab-poc'.
- Egress isolation: iptables on node shows outbound connections only to expected IPs/hostnames.
- Failover: kill PrivateLink ENI (simulate AZ failure) -> check automatic fallback to other endpoint IPs; runtime should reconnect.
- Offline behaviour: disable egress entirely -> runtime transitions to local stub model within 35s and reports event to local logs.

Rollback plan (short & clear):
- If any critical security issue found, steps to isolate nodes immediately:
  1) Remove route for redwood-controlplane.* from VPC route tables (immediate simmer).
  2) K8s: cordon + drain inference nodes (if needed) to stop accepting new traffic.
  3) Revert DNS private zone to point to public control-plane (only in emergency with security team signoff).
  4) For long-term revert: teardown interface endpoints and re-enable NAT-only approach.

Outstanding questions for SLAB security team:
- Are we comfortable with Redwood owning an NLB service consumer side for PrivateLink? They asked to avoid cross-account NLBs; need exact acceptance or we must host endpoints in SLAB account only.
- Confirm whether ECR pulls must go through the same allowlist or SLA allows short-lived pre-signed URLs via S3 endpoint.
- Audit requirement: customer asked for proof of no egress for >30 days — confirm log retention window.

Notes from 2026-02-18 workshop with SLAB (raw):
- Eloise: "We need a way to verify per-instance egress — not just VPC-level; want ephemeral certs on boot."
- Samir: "If PrivateLink is too slow to provision cross-account, do NAT + proxy with strict host header checks."
- Action: Diego to prototype PrivateLink NLB in partner account and share steps in GH PR.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Diego Alvarez: prototype PrivateLink NLB + sample CFN (due 2026-03-15) -> GH PR linked above.
- Samir Patel: prepare security justification doc for interface endpoints (due 2026-03-05) -> attach to Confluence page.
- Maya Chen: finalize test harness for throughput testing across AZs (due 2026-03-10).
- SLAB Sec Ops: confirm final allowlist for third-party services (due 2026-03-01).

Appendix - quick commands / smoke tests:
- DNS: dig +short redwood-controlplane.internal.example @<VPC_DNS_IP>
- TLS check: openssl s_client -connect redwood-controlplane.internal.example:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -servername redwood-controlplane.internal.example
- IPtables check: sudo iptables -L -v -n | grep ESTABLISHED
- S3 throughput test: aws s3 cp s3://slab-models/poc/model.bin /tmp/model.bin --endpoint-url https://s3.amazonaws.com

End of doc.
